The usage of a "to be" ['be' in this case] form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The details were ___ from one person to the other within no time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The details were ___ from one person to the other within no time.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank in the given sentence is 'passed down'. The sentence suggests that information or details were transmitted or conveyed from one person to another. 'Passed down' is the most suitable phrasal verb for this context, as it implies the act of transmitting or handing down information or knowledge from one generation to the next or from one person to another. The other options do not appropriately convey the idea of transferring information from one person to another:

Passed away- typically refers to someone's death.

Passed in-does not convey the intended meaning of transmitting information.

"Passed cut" is not a commonly used phrasal verb and does not convey the intended meaning of transferring information.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

NOTE:

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. I would attach as many as four of them to a crosspiece, notably arranged on a thin spindle, and transmit the motion of the same to a large disc and so derive considerable 'power'. B. In my next attempt I seem to have acted under the first instinctive impulse which later dominated me - to harness the energies of nature to the service of man. C. These creatures were remarkably efficient, for once they started, they had no sense to stop and continued whirling for hours and hours and the hotter it was the harder they worked. D. I did this through the medium of May-bugs - or June-bugs as they are called in America - which were a veritable pest in that country and sometimes broke the branches of trees by the sheer weight of their bodies.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. I would attach as many as four of them to a crosspiece, notably arranged on a thin spindle, and transmit the motion of the same to a large disc and so derive considerable 'power'.

B. In my next attempt I seem to have acted under the first instinctive impulse which later dominated me - to harness the energies of nature to the service of man.

C. These creatures were remarkably efficient, for once they started, they had no sense to stop and continued whirling for hours and hours and the hotter it was the harder they worked.

D. I did this through the medium of May-bugs - or June-bugs as they are called in America - which were a veritable pest in that country and sometimes broke the branches of trees by the sheer weight of their bodies.
questions.solution:
The correct order of the sentences to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph is BDAC. Sentence B comes first as it sets the context for the subsequent actions described in the paragraph. Sentence D introduces the specific method that is used to harness natural energy, highlighting the use of May-bugs. Sentence A further explains the practical application of using the bugs to create power. Sentence C concludes the paragraph by emphasising the efficiency of the May-bugs in generating power continuously.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion hiding in a cave.
options.html: The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion hiding in a cave.

options.text: The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.
options.html: The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.

options.text: An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.
options.html: An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.

options.text: The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion hiding in the cave.
options.html: The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion hiding in the cave.

questions.solution:
The grammatically correct sentence is 'The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave'. This sentence uses the appropriate definite article 'the' before the words 'warrior' and 'lion', indicating specific individuals or entities. Additionally, it correctly uses the phrase 'the right time'. The phrase 'the right time' is the correct choice because it refers to a particular moment that the warrior is waiting for. Using 'an right time' is grammatically incorrect as 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Options (a), (c), and (d) contain grammatical errors. In option (a), 'an right time' should be 'the right time'. Similarly, options (c) and (d) have similar errors with the use of "an" instead of "the" before the words "warrior" and "lion."

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

An article is a word that comes before a noun to indicate whether it's specific or general.

Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.
